description: Direct endpoint attack: send an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) and see if the authorization endpoint accepts and processes it (request object signature bypass).
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept an unsigned (alg=none) request object as an authentic proof of authorization request parameters; if accepted, attacker-controlled parameters may be consumed without integrity verification.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object, indicating request parameter proof integrity may be bypassed.
Control request-object probe returned an invalid HTTP status; environment may not support request objects, making the alg=none result ambiguous.

description: Brokered-flow attack: attempt token exchange using a forged/untrusted subject_token (simulating attacker-signed JWT / trust-anchor substitution) and ensure Dex rejects it; include a control exchange using a valid subject_token from a successful login.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: During token exchange, Dex must verify the submitted subject_token against the configured OIDC connector trust anchor (issuer/JWKS). A forged token must not be consumed as if verified.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute forged-token rejection/acceptance to proof integrity enforcement.
Dex accepted a forged/untrusted subject_token in token exchange, indicating proof integrity failure (verification not applied to consumed token).
Dex returned an identity_id for a forged/untrusted subject_token, suggesting the forged proof was consumed as valid.

description: Config-change + re-auth: enable OIDC connector with insecure_skip_signature_validation=true and demonstrate that attacker-supplied unsigned/forged subject_token can be exchanged (should be rejected in secure configs). Then re-enable with validation and ensure rejection.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Proof integrity depends on signature verification; if signature validation is disabled (misconfiguration), forged proofs may be consumed. When validation is enabled, the same forged proof must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Even with signature validation enabled, Dex accepted a forged/unsigned subject_token, indicating proof integrity failure.
Dex accepted a forged/unsigned subject_token when signature validation was disabled; this demonstrates proof integrity can be broken under insecure configuration.

description: Direct endpoint attack: send unsigned request object (alg=none) that attempts to override critical authorization parameters (redirect_uri/scope/client_id) and check whether Dex accepts it as authoritative.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not consume attacker-controlled authorization parameters from an unsigned request object; if it does, it is verifying a different semantic proof than it consumes.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object as valid input; if processed, this breaks proof integrity by allowing attacker-controlled authorization parameters.
Unsigned request object appears to have been accepted/processed such that the flow proceeded as an authenticated session; request object signature policy may be bypassed.

description: Brokered-flow attack: attempt token exchange with a forged JWT using kid injection (attacker-controlled kid) to trick key selection; include a control exchange using a valid subject_token from a successful password login.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must reject subject_tokens whose signature cannot be verified under the configured OIDC connector trust anchors; kid-based key confusion must not allow acceptance of attacker-signed tokens.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute attacker-token rejection/acceptance to proof integrity enforcement vs setup issues.
Dex accepted an attacker-signed subject_token via kid-based key confusion; signature verification policy may not match consumed proof.

description: Brokered-flow: obtain a valid Dex ID token for user_alice, then attempt token exchange while lying about subject_token_type (treat ID token as access token) to probe token-type confusion in verification vs consumption.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify the exact semantic proof it consumes during token exchange; mislabeling subject_token_type must not cause Dex to validate under a weaker/different policy and still accept the token.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted token exchange when subject_token_type was misrepresented, suggesting verification policy may not match consumed proof semantics (token-type confusion).

description: Direct endpoint I1 test: attempt to supply an unsigned request object (alg=none) that could semantically override/alter critical authorization parameters (scope/state/nonce) compared to the outer query params, probing whether Dex verifies and consumes the same semantic proof.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept or process attacker-controlled unsigned request objects (alg=none), especially when the request object could shadow/override outer authorization parameters; if accepted, verification policy is not applied to the consumed semantic content.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object at the authorization endpoint, indicating proof integrity failure risk (unverified semantic content may be consumed).
Unsigned request object flow appears to have resulted in an authenticated session/identity, suggesting Dex consumed attacker-controlled authorization parameters without proper proof verification.

description: Authorization-code replay: attempt to redeem the same authorization code twice (one-time artifact reuse). Includes a control successful redemption first, then replay redemption.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: An authorization code is a one-time artifact and must not be accepted more than once; the second redemption attempt must fail.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control authorization_code redemption failed; cannot attribute replay outcome to anti-replay enforcement.
Authorization code was accepted more than once (code replay) — one-time artifact reuse.

description: Refresh-token replay: obtain refresh_token for user_alice, rotate it via token exchange/refresh flow, then attempt to reuse the old refresh_token (should be rejected under rotation). Also includes a second identity (user_bob) to ensure multi-identity coverage.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Refresh tokens should not be reusable after rotation; reusing an old refresh token must fail (anti-replay).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control password login failed; cannot evaluate refresh-token replay behavior.
Refresh did not succeed or did not return a refresh token; cannot test old-token replay under rotation.
Old refresh token was accepted after rotation (refresh-token replay) — anti-replay violated.

description: Token-exchange freshness: perform a control token exchange using a valid subject_token, then attempt exchange with an expired subject_token (exp in the past). Uses two identities to ensure distinct sessions and to reduce false positives.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Token exchange must reject expired upstream subject tokens; a token with exp in the past must not be accepted.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; expired-token result would be inconclusive (could be connector/grant/client auth setup).
Token exchange accepted an expired subject_token (exp in the past) — freshness enforcement violated.

description: Replay of a previously issued access token after explicit revocation: token should not remain usable post-revoke (freshness/anti-replay via revocation). Uses two identities to ensure session separation.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: After a session/token is revoked, the same token artifact must not be accepted again (no post-revocation replay).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Post-revocation replay: /userinfo still accepted the revoked session_token (token remained usable after revoke).

description: Replay the same upstream subject_token in RFC8693 token exchange twice. Includes a control exchange and a second identity to ensure connector/client setup is functional. This is a hardening-style I2 check for one-time-use expectations in exchange pipelines.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: If the deployment treats exchanged subject_token artifacts as one-time, the same subject_token should not be accepted for multiple exchanges (anti-replay).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token-exchange replay: the same subject_token was accepted for multiple exchanges (potential anti-replay weakness if one-time semantics are expected).
Control failed: token exchange did not succeed for a fresh subject_token, so replay result is not attributable to freshness enforcement.

description: Authorization code replay across re-authentication: redeem a code once (control), then re-authenticate and attempt to redeem the same code again. Uses two identities and re-auth to ensure the replay is not a transient session artifact.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Authorization codes are one-time artifacts; once redeemed, the same code must not be accepted again even after re-authentication.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code replay: the same code was accepted more than once (one-time artifact reuse).

description: Authorization-code one-time artifact replay after revoking the first session: redeem code once (control), revoke resulting session, then attempt to redeem the same code again.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: An authorization code is a one-time artifact and must not be redeemable more than once, even if the first resulting session is revoked.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: initial authorization_code exchange did not succeed, so replay result is not attributable to anti-replay enforcement.
Authorization code was accepted more than once (replay succeeded) even after revoking the first session; one-time artifact anti-replay violated.

description: RFC8693 token exchange: perform a control exchange with a valid subject_token, then attempt exchange with a subject_token that has nbf far in the future (should be rejected). Includes a second identity control to reduce false positives.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Token exchange must reject subject tokens that are not yet valid (nbf in the future), while accepting a valid control token under the same connector/client context.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: token exchange with a valid subject_token did not succeed; future-nbf rejection cannot be attributed to freshness enforcement.
Token exchange accepted a subject_token with nbf in the future; not-yet-valid token was treated as fresh/valid.

description: Attempt to replay an authorization code obtained in one identity context after a separate identity authenticates, probing whether code redemption is improperly reusable across time/session boundaries.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Authorization codes must be single-use and must not remain redeemable after a different user completes a separate login flow (anti-replay across sessions).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: Alice initial code exchange did not succeed; replay test is not valid.
Control failed: Bob login flow did not succeed; cross-session replay test is not valid.
Authorization code remained redeemable after another user completed a separate flow; one-time artifact anti-replay violated.

description: I2 anti-replay: reuse an old access token after a second login (re-auth) to see if prior token is improperly invalidated or remains usable beyond intended session semantics
invariant_hypothesis: I2: If the deployment intends single-session semantics for password-grant tokens, an access token from a prior login should not remain usable after a subsequent re-authentication event for the same principal; otherwise tokens are replayable beyond intended lifetime/session boundary.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control logins failed; cannot attribute any token reuse behavior to freshness/anti-replay enforcement.
Alice and Bob mapped to the same downstream identity; cannot reason about replay boundaries across principals.
Old Alice session token remained usable after a subsequent re-authentication, indicating potential replay beyond intended session boundary.

description: Attempt to redeem an authorization code without client authentication (no client_secret) and without PKCE verifier, probing whether the code is improperly unbound from the client/session.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the correct client authentication context; redeeming a code without client auth (and without PKCE) must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control authorization-code exchange failed; cannot attribute attack outcome to client-binding enforcement.
Authorization code was redeemable without client authentication (and without PKCE verifier), indicating broken flow coherence/client binding.

description: Redeem a valid authorization code using a different redirect_uri than was used at authorization time, probing whether Dex enforces redirect_uri binding during token exchange.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The authorization code must be bound to the original redirect_uri; redemption with a mismatched redirect_uri must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control exchange failed; cannot interpret redirect_uri mismatch outcome.
Authorization code was redeemable with a mismatched redirect_uri, indicating broken flow coherence (redirect_uri binding not enforced).

description: Probe state-swap/cross-session splicing by initiating two parallel auth requests with different state values and attempting to complete the flow using the other session's state/code pairing.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The authorization response must be bound to the initiating browser session and its state; cross-session state/code splicing must not yield a valid token.

oracle_checks.assertion: alice_state_control_exchange_http_status == 200 AND bob_state_control_exchange_http_status == 200 AND user_alice_state_control_http_status == 200 AND user_bob_state_control_http_status == 200
oracle_checks.violation_description: One or both control flows failed; cannot attribute state-swap outcome to flow coherence enforcement.
Token endpoint accepted a cross-session spliced redemption (code from one session with verifier from another), indicating broken flow coherence/session binding.

description: Attempt to splice PKCE parameters via unsigned request object: send code_challenge in request object, then redeem code without code_verifier. Expect token exchange rejection (flow should be coherent if PKCE was accepted/required).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: If the authorization request establishes PKCE semantics (code_challenge), the token endpoint must enforce the corresponding code_verifier binding; otherwise the flow can be completed out-of-order/without required step.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token endpoint accepted an authorization_code redemption without code_verifier after a request that included code_challenge, indicating possible step-skipping / broken PKCE binding.

description: Probe connector-binding coherence in RFC8693 token exchange: obtain a subject_token via one login context, then attempt token_exchange under a different identity context to see if the exchange improperly ignores session/client binding.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Token exchange must be bound to the authenticated client/session context and connector; a subject_token from one context should not be splicable into another session to mint tokens.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange succeeded using a subject_token from a different authenticated identity context, suggesting cross-session splicing in the exchange flow.

description: Probe token-exchange flow coherence by omitting connector_id (required by Dex) while presenting a valid subject_token from a different identity context.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Token exchange must be bound to the intended connector/session context; missing connector_id must not be accepted because it would allow step-skipping/ambiguous upstream binding.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange succeeded without connector_id, suggesting the exchange flow is not coherently bound to a specific upstream connector context.

description: Attempt to override redirect_uri via an unsigned request object (alg=none) to probe whether Dex processes attacker-controlled request-object parameters inconsistently with the outer query, enabling flow splicing.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization request parameters must be coherently bound; if request objects are accepted, the effective redirect_uri/state must not be attacker-overridable in a way that breaks the expected FSM and session binding.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) was accepted, increasing risk of parameter override/splicing that can break flow coherence.

description: Code injection / cross-session splicing: obtain an authorization code in victim's browser session, then attempt to redeem that code from an attacker context (different user session) to see if Dex binds the code to the initiating session/user.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization codes must be bound to the correct browser session/user flow; a code minted for victim's session must not be redeemable by an attacker session (no cross-session splicing).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: victim could not redeem their own authorization code; cannot attribute attack outcome to flow coherence.
Dex allowed attacker context to redeem victim's authorization code (cross-session code injection / flow splicing).

description: Case confusion in username: attempt to authenticate as two security-distinct principals whose usernames differ only by case and verify Dex does not collapse them into one downstream identity.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Security-distinct upstream principals (e.g., 'Admin' vs 'admin') must not map to the same downstream subject/identity due to case-folding or normalization.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Case-variant principals collapsed to the same normalized username (preferred_username), risking identity confusion
UserInfo verification failed for one or both sessions; identity comparison is inconclusive

description: Cross-protocol identity merge: obtain a session via password grant, then obtain another session via RFC8693 token exchange using the first session's token as subject_token; verify the exchanged identity does not collapse into the original principal unexpectedly.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Distinct upstream principals/contexts (password-authenticated principal vs token-exchange derived principal) must not collapse into the same downstream identity unless explicitly intended by broker policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Token exchange produced a session that collapses into the same downstream identity as the password principal, indicating potential principal-binding confusion across auth contexts
UserInfo verification failed for one or both sessions; identity comparison is inconclusive

description: Probe whether an empty/blank upstream principal identifier collapses to a default/anonymous subject shared across users (empty_sub collision).
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Two security-distinct upstream principals (normal username vs empty username) must not map to the same downstream identity; empty identifiers must not fall back to a shared subject.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals

oracle_checks.assertion: user_empty_sub_http_status >= 400 OR (user_empty_sub_entity_id != user_A_entity_id AND user_empty_sub_entity_id != user_B_entity_id)
oracle_checks.violation_description: Empty-subject login was accepted and collapsed into an existing principal (or a shared default identity) instead of being rejected or mapped distinctly

description: Probe whether groups claim type confusion (string vs array) causes principal mapping collapse or mis-binding in downstream identity (type_confusion_groups).
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Two security-distinct upstream principals with different group-claim encodings must not collapse into the same downstream identity due to claim parsing/type confusion.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals

oracle_checks.assertion: user_A_groups_string_http_status >= 400 OR user_B_groups_array_http_status >= 400 OR user_A_groups_string_entity_id != user_B_groups_array_entity_id
oracle_checks.violation_description: Type-confused group claim handling caused two distinct principals to collapse into the same downstream identity

description: Probe cross-connector identity merge: two distinct upstream principals (different connector_id) sharing the same email should not collapse into one downstream identity unless explicitly intended by broker policy.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Security-distinct upstream principals from different connectors must not be merged into the same downstream subject solely due to shared email/username-like attributes.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals

oracle_checks.assertion: user_A_via_exchange_http_status >= 400 OR user_B_via_exchange_http_status >= 400 OR user_A_via_exchange_entity_id != user_B_via_exchange_entity_id
oracle_checks.violation_description: Distinct principals collapsed into the same downstream identity after brokered/token-exchange flow, suggesting merge-by-attribute (e.g., email) rather than stable principal binding

description: I4 attack: attempt to collapse two distinct upstream principals by forcing identical preferred_username via OIDC request parameters (login_hint/id_token_hint) and observe downstream identity mapping.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Two security-distinct upstream principals must not map to the same downstream identity even if attacker-controlled hints try to coerce the same username.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Two distinct principals collapsed into one downstream identity when attacker supplied identical login_hint/id_token_hint values

description: I4 attack: attempt to force identity merge by using two distinct password principals that share the same email-like identifier format and see if Dex collapses them by email rather than stable subject.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Distinct upstream principals must not be merged solely due to matching email-like attributes or formatting tricks.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Re-authentication of one principal merged/collapsed into the other principal's downstream identity (email/alias-based merge)

description: Attempt principal collapse by swapping subject_token between two distinct password principals during RFC8693 token exchange and checking whether Dex mis-binds the resulting identity to the wrong upstream principal.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Two security-distinct upstream principals (alice vs bob) must not collapse into the same downstream identity, even when their tokens are used as subject_token in token exchange.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Token exchange mis-bound principal: exchanging with Bob's subject_token did not map to Bob (or collapsed identities), indicating principal binding confusion
Token exchange mis-bound principal: exchanging with Alice's subject_token did not map to Alice (or collapsed identities), indicating principal binding confusion

description: Token-exchange scope escalation: start with minimal OIDC scope, then attempt RFC8693 token exchange requesting expanded scopes (groups/profile/federated:id) and verify extra claims are not granted.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Exchanged tokens must not contain claims/permissions beyond the upstream authorization intent (original scopes) and broker policy; requesting broader scopes at token_exchange must be rejected or not yield extra claims.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange granted expanded-scope group claims (or succeeded when it should have been constrained to original openid email intent).
Token exchange produced a token bound to a different principal than the upstream intent, risking over-grant via mis-binding.

description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) attempt to override authorization parameters (scope/redirect_uri) and gain broader effective permissions than intended.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Authorization parameters (especially scope) must be bound to authenticated client intent and broker policy; an unsigned request object must not be accepted to expand scopes or alter redirect_uri.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned request object (alg=none), enabling attacker-controlled parameter injection and potential scope escalation.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_reqobj_control_http_status < 400 AND user_reqobj_control_http_status is not None
oracle_checks.violation_description: Control authorization-code flow failed; cannot attribute request-object behavior to security enforcement vs misconfiguration.

description: Attempt to use password grant to request broader scopes than intended (groups/profile/federated:id/offline_access) and verify Dex does not grant extra claims/refresh token beyond broker policy.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Even if password grant is enabled, requested scopes must be constrained by BrokerPolicy(config); requesting expanded scopes must not yield extra identity claims or refresh tokens if not allowed.

params.scope: openid email groups profile federated:id offline_access

oracle_checks.violation_description: Password grant accepted expanded scopes and issued refresh_token (offline_access) without clear broker policy allowance, risking authorization over-grant.
Expanded-scope password grant resulted in groups claims being granted unexpectedly, indicating scope/authorization binding failure.

description: Attempt RFC8693 token exchange using only body client_id/client_secret (no HTTP Basic) to see if Dex mis-binds the client and issues a token anyway, potentially exceeding BrokerPolicy(client auth requirements). Includes a control exchange using the same subject_token.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must be bound to an authenticated client per broker policy; if client authentication is bypassed (e.g., body creds accepted when Basic is required), effective permissions may exceed intended client authorization.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted token exchange when client authentication should require HTTP Basic; this can allow unauthorized clients to obtain tokens (authorization binding failure).
Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute attack failure/success to authorization binding enforcement.
